mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with positive economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns when UNRATE is below 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which tends to stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate increases and the federal funds rate also increases, it may signal tightening economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS increase, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth, indicated by a decline in GDPC1, suggests weakening demand, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns when GDPC1 growth is below 2%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production, as indicated by INDPRO, signals strong economic activity, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns when INDPRO is increasing, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real sales, as indicated by RSAFS, suggests weakening consumer demand, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns when RSAFS is below $350 billion, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts increase but payroll employment does not, it may indicate an imbalance in economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST increases but PAYEMS does not, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A high rate of inflation, as indicated by CPIAUCSL, may lead to tighter monetary policy, which is likely to result in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns when CPIAUCSL is above 3%, this hypothesis is rejected.
